Corporate Governance and the King IV Paradigm

For a diversified technology holding company, governance is not merely a box-ticking exercise but a vital tool for ensuring long-term sustainability. The King IV Code advocates for an "apply and explain" methodology, requiring the Veramani board to demonstrate how its governance practices achieve outcomes such as effective control and legitimacy [cite: 2, 14].

Key governance structures essential for an IT holding company include specialized committees that oversee the high-stakes sectors of its subsidiaries [cite: 14]. Its primary mandate is to manage a diverse array of specialized subsidiaries that collectively provide an end-to-end industrial technology stack, specifically targeted at the mining and telecommunications sectors [cite: 16, 17, 18].

## 1. Veramani IT Division: The Orchestration and AI Fabric

Veramani IT is the "central brain" of the group, responsible for architecting the overarching AI and data architecture for the 16 Veralogix companies [cite: 16, 19]. Its core mission is the deployment of a sovereign AI fabric that ingests data from disparate sources—including Odoo ERP, field telemetry, and site reports—into a unified corporate knowledge graph [cite: 16].

| Relationship Pillar | Implementation Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| Trading Relationship | Provides high-level management and AI-agentic orchestration for all group subsidiaries [cite: 16]. |
| Revenue Flow Model | Management fees and shared service charges billed to operating entities based on usage of the AI fabric [cite: 20, 21]. |
| Shared Services | Manages the central retrieval spine, corporate knowledge graphs, and agentic dispatch system [cite: 16]. |

Veramani has recently expanded its operational footprint into India (Veramanie Technologies PvT), establishing a dedicated team of red, blue, and purple security teams alongside app and web development verticals [cite: 22, 23].
